sections.content:
You know *según* + a source from B1 Unit 13, *conforme a* from B2 Unit 27 and *como si* from B2 Unit 15. New here: *como* and *según* followed by a verb, to say how something is done.

• *como* + verb: "the way", "however".
• *según* + verb: "as", or "depending on how".

The mood tells the listener whether the way is known. When the way is a fact (someone told you, or you know it), the verb is in the indicative: *Lo hice como me lo explicaron.* When the way is open and someone can still choose, the verb is in the subjunctive: *Hazlo como quieras.*

sections.title: Known way, open way
rows: Prepara el café como te enseñé.
Make the coffee the way I showed you.
Make the coffee however you like.
I cooked it as they told me.
Elige la fecha según te parezca mejor.
Choose the date as it seems best to you.

sections.content: *Como si* is different: it compares with something unreal and takes the imperfect subjunctive (B2 Unit 15). *Como quieras* has no *si* and is about a real choice.
